title: Annihilator of a finite module under flat base change
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a flat map of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and let $M$ be a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Then the annihilator of the base-changed module [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] is the extended annihilator: $\operatorname{Ann}_S(M\otimes_R S)=\operatorname{Ann}_R(M)S$, where $\operatorname{Ann}_R(M)=\{r\in R:rm=0\text{ for every }m\in M\}$ and $\operatorname{Ann}_R(M)S$ is the ideal generated by the image of $\operatorname{Ann}_R(M)$ in $S$.

source.place: Tag 07T8, lemma-annihilator-flat-base-change, second assertion for a finite module.

proof.text: Write $\varphi:R\to S$ for the given map, and choose generators $m_1,\ldots,m_n$ of $M$ using [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; by adjoining a zero generator we may take $n\geq1$, even when $M=0$. Put $I=\operatorname{Ann}_R(M)$ and define the $R$-linear map $u:R\to M^n$ by $u(r)=(rm_1,\ldots,rm_n)$. An element $r$ lies in $\ker u$ exactly when it kills every $m_i$; then it kills every sum $\sum_i a_i m_i$, hence all of $M$. Thus $\ker u=I$, and with $\iota:I\hookrightarrow R$ the inclusion, $0\to I\xrightarrow{\iota}R\xrightarrow{u}M^n$ is exact.

source.place: Tag 07T8 (lemma-annihilator-flat-base-change), proof of the finite-module assertion, combining the generator maps into a finite product; compare Tag 0BBY (lemma-flat-intersect-ideals), proof by tensoring a simultaneous kernel sequence.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], $S$ is flat as an $R$-module. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] to the exact sequence of Step 1. It gives the exact sequence $0\to I\otimes_R S\xrightarrow{\iota\otimes1}R\otimes_R S\xrightarrow{u\otimes1}M^n\otimes_R S$. No flatness or finite presentation of $M$ or $I$ is required.

source.place: Tag 07T8 (lemma-annihilator-flat-base-change), proof of the finite-module assertion, combining the generator maps into a finite product; compare Tag 0BBY (lemma-flat-intersect-ideals), proof by tensoring a simultaneous kernel sequence.

proof.text: The tensor relations of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] identify $R\otimes_R S$ with $S$ by $r\otimes s\mapsto\varphi(r)s$, with inverse $s\mapsto1\otimes s$: the composites are identities since $r\otimes s=1\otimes\varphi(r)s$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-finite-product], identify $M^n\otimes_R S$ with $(M\otimes_R S)^n$ by $(x_i)_i\otimes s\mapsto(x_i\otimes s)_i$. The map $u\otimes1$ therefore becomes $v:S\to(M\otimes_R S)^n$, $s\mapsto(m_i\otimes s)_i$, as can be checked on $1\otimes s$. The first map becomes $\alpha:I\otimes_R S\to S$, $a\otimes s\mapsto\varphi(a)s$. As tensors are finite sums of pure tensors, its image is precisely the set of finite sums $\sum_j\varphi(a_j)s_j$ with $a_j\in I$, namely $IS$. Exactness from Step 2 now gives $\ker v=IS$.

source.place: Tag 07T8 (lemma-annihilator-flat-base-change), proof of the finite-module assertion, combining the generator maps into a finite product; compare Tag 0BBY (lemma-flat-intersect-ideals), proof by tensoring a simultaneous kernel sequence.

proof.text: The elements $m_i\otimes1$ generate $M\otimes_R S$ over $S$: for a pure tensor write $m=\sum_i a_i m_i$ and use the tensor relations [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] to obtain $m\otimes s=\sum_i(m_i\otimes\varphi(a_i)s)=\sum_i\varphi(a_i)s\,(m_i\otimes1)$; every tensor is a finite sum of these. Thus an $s\in S$ kills all of $M\otimes_R S$ if and only if it kills each $m_i\otimes1$, equivalently $m_i\otimes s=0$ for every $i$, equivalently $s\in\ker v$. Step 3 gives $\operatorname{Ann}_S(M\otimes_R S)=\ker v=IS=\operatorname{Ann}_R(M)S$.
